title: Ça peut te valoir un César  (That Could Win You a César)

segments.t: Gabriel talks to Julie in her dressing room while Andrea hears JoeyStarr's complaints outside. Gabriel appeals to the film's possible rewards; JoeyStarr mocks Julie's grand manner and musical interests. Listen to the French first, and notice how each speaker tries to make a point.
Je ne retourne pas sur ce plateau!
Il doit s'excuser avant!
J'ai travaillé dur pour ce rôle. J'ai étudié l'époque!
Et lui, il improvise!
Reste calme, Julie. Pense à ta carrière.
Un film en costumes, c'est difficile à tourner.
Mais ça peut te valoir un César! Au minimum!
Ça vaut bien un petit effort.
Non, Julie!
Vous avez entendu son accent, sa façon de parler?
Elle se prend pour le prince Charles?
Elle prend des cours de musique ancienne!
Elle dit toujours: oui, j'adore la musique de Bach!
Julie explains to Gabriel why she refuses to return. He tries to turn her thoughts back to her career.
Je ne retourne pas sur ce plateau!
'I'm not going back onto that set!' The present tense makes the refusal sound immediate and definite. The word for this singles out the set she refuses to return to.
Il doit s'excuser avant!
'He has to apologise first!' The action means apologise, and French gives it a reflexive form: excuse oneself. Before refers back to returning to work, so it means first here.
J'ai travaillé dur pour ce rôle. J'ai étudié l'époque!
'I worked hard for this part. I studied the period!' Both actions are completed in the past. The word for hard describes how she worked, while the period is the historical setting she studied.
Et lui, il improvise!
'And he just improvises!' The strong word for him comes before the ordinary subject he. Repeating the person this way gives extra emphasis to the contrast with her preparation.
Reste calme, Julie. Pense à ta carrière.
'Stay calm, Julie. Think of your career.' These two familiar instructions ask her to stay calm and think. Thinking of someone or something uses the small connecting word also often translated as to.
Un film en costumes, c'est difficile à tourner.
'A costume drama is difficult to shoot.' The French expression literally says a film in costumes. The action word that normally means turn can also mean shoot when the object is a film.
Mais ça peut te valoir un César! Au minimum!
'But that could win you a César! At least!' The action means earn or bring someone a result. The little word for you identifies who could receive the French film award.
Ça vaut bien un petit effort.
'It's well worth a little effort.' Now the same action word means be worth. Well strengthens the judgment that a little effort is a reasonable price for that possible reward.
Non, Julie!
'No, Julie!' A short no followed by someone's name can protest or try to stop them. Gabriel is trying to keep Julie in the conversation.
Vous avez entendu son accent, sa façon de parler?
'Have you heard her accent, her way of speaking?' The completed past question asks whether they have heard something. A way of speaking is built from the noun way followed by of and the action speak.
Elle se prend pour le prince Charles?
'Does she think she's Prince Charles?' The expression literally says she takes herself for someone. It suggests pretension: he thinks her grand way of speaking is an act.
Elle prend des cours de musique ancienne!
'She takes lessons in old music!' The word for lessons is plural even though it ends in the same letter in the singular. Early music describes music from an older historical tradition.
Elle dit toujours: oui, j'adore la musique de Bach!

'She always says: yes, I love Bach's music!' The action for love is stronger than simply like. He imitates her enthusiasm for the composer to ridicule her cultivated taste. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more.
Je ne retourne pas sur ce plateau!
Il doit s'excuser avant!
J'ai travaillé dur pour ce rôle. J'ai étudié l'époque!
Et lui, il improvise!
Reste calme, Julie. Pense à ta carrière.
Un film en costumes, c'est difficile à tourner.
Mais ça peut te valoir un César! Au minimum!
Ça vaut bien un petit effort.
Non, Julie!
Vous avez entendu son accent, sa façon de parler?
Elle se prend pour le prince Charles?
Elle prend des cours de musique ancienne!
Elle dit toujours: oui, j'adore la musique de Bach!

Gabriel argues that the film is worth the effort, while JoeyStarr is still making fun of his co-star outside. You have heard two useful senses of the action meaning to be worth or to earn someone a reward. See you next time.
À demain!
